subject: Next steps: hosting fit and clarifications on SSO / KMS / log retention
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + clarifying integration asks (SSO / KMS / logs)

Hi Amelia — thanks for the thoughtful conversation today. Two quick recaps and asks so we can map the right hosting path for QuantaPlane: 

Summary from our call:
- Primary constraint: compliance for customer data (ePHI) and auditability.
- Identity: your security team requires SAML 2.0 SSO plus SCIM for provisioning (Okta + Azure AD supported).
- Key management: you indicated a requirement for customer-controlled keys backed by an HSM (preference for dedicated HSM / on-prem key custody).
- Logging: need long-term audit retention and ability to push logs to your SIEM; retention policy is a key decision driver.
- Traffic profile: interactive inference with occasional bulk embeddings; latency SLOs are important.

Immediate clarifying questions we need answered to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: 
1) For KMS/HSM: do you require the HSM to be physically on-prem (direct HSM), or would a cloud KMS with an external key manager (EKM) / customer-managed key in the cloud meet your policy?
2) For logs: what is the target retention window on your side (months/years)? Do you require us to retain full request logs longer than 90 days?
3) Identity provisioning: is IdP-initiated SSO required in addition to SP-initiated flows? Any specific SCIM attribute expectations?
4) Networking: are you able to accept VPC peering / private networking to a Dedicated deployment, or is full air-gapped/on-prem required?

Next steps I propose:
- You reply to the three quick clarifying items above.
- We schedule a 30-min follow-up with our Solutions Engineer to demo our KMS integration options (cloud EKM flow + Private HSM option) and show log-forwarding to Splunk/Datadog.
- I'll attach our SOC2 and a short one-pager on deploy options for your security/procurement teams.

Attachments: SOC2-type2-2025.pdf (stub), redwood-deploy-options-onepager.pdf (stub)

Thanks,

Ben — thanks for the summary and for sending the SOC2. Quick answers below so you can scope: 

1) KMS/HSM: Policy requires customer control of keys and hardware-backed protection. Preferred is on-prem HSM or a cloud EKM that allows us to control key material in our HSM appliance. We cannot accept vendor-managed keys without HSM custody.

2) Logs: We need audit logs retained for 7 years for regulatory audits (healthcare). It's OK if Redwood retains only 90 days of vendor-side logs provided we can export and retain logs in our SIEM for the long term. We also need assurance that request/response metadata required for audits (timestamp, request id, model version, token counts) can be included in forwarded logs.

3) Identity: We need both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SSO. SCIM provisioning required; must support Okta and Azure AD as attributes: email, displayName, active, groups.

4) Networking: We'd prefer Dedicated with private networking if it meets the KMS/HSM requirement. If Dedicated cannot integrate with our HSM/EKM model, we will require a Private (customer-managed) deployment.

Other notes: procurement would like a short checklist of what distinguishes Dedicated vs Private from an integration and timeline perspective. Also please send an initial estimate of latency SLOs (P50/P95) for Dedicated vs Private for our expected profile (avg 2–4 concurrent interactive sessions, intermittent batched embeddings).

Happy to loop in our procurement lead to set up contract review once the technical fits are clear.

Best,
Amelia Zhang
Head of Platform Security, QuantaPlane
amelia@quantaplane.com

Thanks for the forward, Ben — quick technical breakdown and proposed next steps below. I kept this in checklist form so you can send to procurement/security.

1) Identity (SSO / SCIM)
- We support SAML 2.0 with both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows for Hosted (where applicable), Dedicated, and Private.
- SCIM provisioning (v2) is supported on Dedicated and Private with Okta and Azure AD verified attribute mappings (email, displayName, active, groups). For Hosted API customers we offer SCIM for organizations on our Enterprise plan (dedicated control plane).

2) KMS / HSM options
- Hosted API: Redwood-managed keys only (not acceptable per customer requirement).
- Dedicated: supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS + EKM (bring-your-own-key flow) in supported cloud regions. This allows key material to be controlled by the customer HSM/EKM and used by Redwood services. Supported partners: AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed keys (via EKM), Google Cloud External KMS partners, and Azure Key Vault with HSM-protected keys. Integration requires network connectivity (VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud) and a short crypto handshake setup.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full support for direct HSM integration where the HSM appliance can be colocated/on-prem and keys never leave customer control. This is the option we recommend if the customer's policy strictly requires physical on-prem HSM custody.

Implication: If QuantaPlane can accept a cloud-EKM model where the key material is controlled by their HSM/EKM, Dedicated is viable. If they insist on a physically on-prem HSM with no cloud EKM allowed, Private is required.

3) Logs & retention
- Redwood can export ingest-level logs (request id, timestamp, model version, token counts, user id hash, processing latency) to customer SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, S3 export) in near-real time.
- Vendor-side retention default: 90 days for full request/response payloads. We can redact or truncate payloads on request.
- Customer-side retention: we provide log-forwarding and export hooks; customers are responsible for long-term retention (7 years) in their own storage.
- For auditability: we can provide a signed export (hash chain) and delivery receipts for compliance purposes as part of the Private or Dedicated EKM integration.

4) Latency SLOs (rough estimates for their profile)
- Dedicated (with VPC peering): P50 ~ 20–30ms token inference (depends on model), P95 ~ 80–200ms depending on burst and sequence length.
- Private (on-prem): P50 ~ 10–20ms (local network advantage), P95 ~ 50–120ms.
- Note: exact numbers depend on model size and instance class; we'll validate during the SE demo.

5) Proposed next steps / timeline
- SE demo (30–45 min): demo Dedicated EKM flow + log-forwarding (we can show a test integration to their Okta + KMS). Target: within 5 business days.
- Procurement checklist: I'll draft the Dedicated vs Private checklist and network/KMS requirements and share by EOD Thursday (3 business days).
- Private estimate: standard Private-onboarding timeline is 2–3 weeks for planning + 3–5 weeks delivery depending on network approvals and customer infra readiness.

I'll prepare the short comparison doc and a network/KMS diagram (attach) and we'll include Rishi on the SE call to cover cloud KMS vendors we support.

Laura Bennett
